correctness.rationale: PASS. The graph has ten vertices and fifteen edges; a graph Morse face is exactly an acyclic partial orientation with at most one outgoing edge per vertex. The attached finite exhaustive enumeration reconstructs 314,928 faces, and its bitmask incidence face poset is validated against independent rooted-forest Laplacian counts. The explicitly ordered 157,259 augmented Morse pairs yield exactly 77 critical seven-cells and 333 critical eight-cells; unpairing the empty face creates one critical vertex, and an exhaustive topological sort checks acyclicity on 2,099,520 directed face incidences. The signed integral Morse boundary is 77-by-333, has 235 nonzero entries of absolute value one, and reduces by exactly 39 unit row/column pivots to a zero residual matrix. Since the critical seven-skeleton is a wedge of 77 seven-spheres and pi_7 equals Z^77, the unit diagonal form gives 39 homotopy cancellations, proving the wedge of 38 seven-spheres and 294 eight-spheres. Both extracted standalone verifiers were run. The finite statement asserts no family-wide theorem.

originality.rationale: PASS with specified residual risk. The closest exact public item concerns precisely the Petersen ordinary Morse complex but proves only reduced mod-two Betti numbers 38 and 294, explicitly not integral homology or homotopy. Finite Betti numbers over F_2 do not imply an integral wedge-of-spheres decomposition or control eight-cell attaching maps. The full-text checked Chari-Joswig foundational theorem, Donovan-Lin-Scoville leaf/family results, and Scoville-Zaremsky connectivity bounds do not determine the Petersen integral attaching matrix; Kozlov addresses related simple-homotopy graph complexes, not this exact object. Alternative constructions such as edge matching, 2-matching and strong Morse complexes were distinguished by definitions. No covering published statement was located; an unindexed or unpublished equivalent result remains possible.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent integral homotopy computation may exist in unindexed, unpublished, or poorly indexed literature; no search can prove global originality.
A recent paper on strong discrete-Morse matchings, arXiv:2609.06844, could not be retrieved in full here, though its strongly restricted simplicial object differs from the ordinary Morse complex.
The finite integer computations have been reproduced locally, not independently audited by a third party; any implementation error in the verifiers would be a residual reproducibility risk.

value.rationale: PASS. The Petersen graph is a canonical vertex-transitive cubic graph, and its full ordinary Morse complex is a natural rooted-forest topology object. An exact published mod-two computation left torsion and integral homotopy unresolved. The new 39-unit attaching-map cancellation settles both and gives a complete mixed-dimensional wedge type, a structurally meaningful classification distinct from known numerical Betti values and stronger than generic connectivity bounds.
